newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL COFFEE COOL AT WEEKEND BUT NO DAMAGING COLD.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL COFFEE COOL AT WEEKEND BUT NO DAMAGING COLD.

text.p: Brazil's coffee regions saw cool temperatures over the weekend but no damaging cold, and temperatures should pick up over the coming days, local meteorologists Somar said Sunday.

Minimum temperatures of around eight degrees Celsius were reported by cooperatives in northern Parana over the weekend, while in Pocos de Caldas, southern Minas Gerais, the low early Sunday morning was six degrees Celsius, the local cooperative said.
Pocos de Caldas is traditionally one of Brazil's coldest coffee areas, but temperatures did dip to four degrees Celsius in some parts of southern Minas Gerais, said Somar forecaster Marcio Custodio.
The cool weather was the tail end of a polar air mass which has moved out to sea.

The next polar air mass is expected to arrive in the south of the country on Tuesday, but it is of weak intensity with a center of 1,026 millibars and will only affect the far east of the southeast region later in the week, posing no threat to coffee, Custodio said.
At this stage of the winter, it is now hard to imagine any further threat of frost to coffee regions, he added. ((-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151))
